extracted.intended_audience: Investigators and research teams preparing grant applications to the CDMRP Vision Research Program (VRP); researchers in vision trauma, military medicine, and translational ophthalmic research
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare a research proposal for the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs Vision Research Program (VRP) that addresses military-relevant eye injury or visual dysfunction and aligns with the program's mission and priorities. Proposals should be innovative, clinically relevant, and enable delivery of care in military operational environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with VRP mission and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Transform visual system trauma care for our armed forces and the nation' and 'Address clinical needs through innovative research targeting the mechanism, effects, and treatment of service-connected eye injuries and vision dysfunction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should clearly state how the proposed work maps to the VRP mission and scope: focus on military-related eye injuries or vision dysfunction, and explain how outcomes will address clinical needs for Service Members, Veterans, and military healthcare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to military exposure and service‑connected vision problems
rubrics_metrics.description: '...eye injury or visual dysfunction associated with military exposure' (including visual sequelae of traumatic brain injury).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must tie the research question or intervention explicitly to military exposures or service‑connected conditions (e.g., blast, combat trauma, TBI-associated visual dysfunction). Describe the target population and why findings will be applicable to Service Members/Veterans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (novelty of approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The VRP challenges the scientific community to design innovative research'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate novelty compared to current state-of-the-art (concepts, methods, technologies, or applications). Describe what is new, how it differs from existing approaches, and why the innovative element is likely to yield improved outcomes or understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant advancement / impact
rubrics_metrics.description: '...that will significantly advance the understanding, prevention, diagnosis, mitigation, and/or treatment of eye injury or visual dysfunction'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate expected impact at scientific, clinical, or operational levels. Explain how results will advance knowledge, change clinical practice, improve prevention/diagnosis/mitigation/treatment, or otherwise produce measurable benefit for military populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational and operational relevance (enable delivery of care)
rubrics_metrics.description: '...research that will enable the delivery of care in the military operational environment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize feasibility, portability, durability, resource constraints, or other considerations relevant to delivering the intervention or diagnostic in deployed/operational settings. Describe steps toward translation, implementation, or transition to military care systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on targeted research domains (mechanism, effects, prevention, diagnosis, mitigation, treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The program targets research 'targeting the mechanism, effects, and treatment' and more broadly prevention, diagnosis, and mitigation of vision injury and dysfunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which domain(s) the proposal addresses (e.g., mechanistic studies, diagnostics, therapeutics, mitigation strategies, prevention) and tailor aims, methods, and outcomes to that domain. Ensure objectives are appropriate for the chosen domain and will produce relevant deliverables or knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to military/DOD-specific research guidance and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources listed for investigators include 'A Beginner's Guide to Army Healthcare System', 'Blast Term Dictionary and Guidance Documents for Blast Injury Research', and 'A Primer for Conducting DOD Funded Human Research with Military Populations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate awareness of and compliance with DOD/military research policies and terminology. Use recommended guidance documents where applicable (e.g., for blast-related research, human subjects policies, or navigating military healthcare systems). Describe protections, consent, and procedures specific to military populations when applicable.
